  - main:
    - heading "Use FaceTime on your iPhone or iPad" [level=1]
    - paragraph: With FaceTime, you can make and answer calls, translate different languages, share your screen, watch movies together, and more—all in real time.
    - paragraph:
      - link "Make a FaceTime call ":
        - /url: "#make-call"
    - paragraph:
      - link "Answer a FaceTime call ":
        - /url: "#audio"
    - paragraph:
      - link "Discover more ways to interact on a FaceTime call ":
        - /url: "#options"
    - paragraph:
      - link "Find your missed calls, voicemails, and more in FaceTime ":
        - /url: "#Find"
    - heading "Make a FaceTime call" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - paragraph: In Settings, scroll to Apps, then tap FaceTime.
      - listitem:
        - paragraph:
          - text: Tap to
          - link "This links to the iPhone user guide section about setting up FaceTime.":
            - /url: https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/get-started-with-facetime-iphc4774d8d8/ios
            - text: turn on FaceTime
          - text: .
      - listitem:
        - paragraph:
          - text: Then, in the FaceTime app (not Settings), tap the New Call button. If you have the person's phone number or email address saved in your Contacts,
          - superscript: "1"
          - text: start typing their name and tap the name when it appears.
      - listitem:
        - paragraph: Tap the Audio button or the FaceTime button to start the call.
        - img "In FaceTime on iPhone, a name is entered in the To field for a new FaceTime call."
    - paragraph:
      - text: You can use FaceTime over Wi-Fi
      - superscript: "2"
      - text: or over cellular on supported iOS or iPadOS devices.
      - superscript: "3"
      - text: Data rates may apply. FaceTime, Group FaceTime, or FaceTime audio may not be available in all countries or regions.
    - heading "Answer a FaceTime call" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - paragraph: If you see an incoming FaceTime call, tap the Accept button to answer.
        - img "iPhone home screen showing a FaceTime Video call with the option to accept or decline."
      - listitem:
        - paragraph: "If you're already on FaceTime, and you get another incoming call, tap one of these options:"
        - list:
          - listitem:
            - paragraph: End & Accept (ends your current call and accepts the incoming call)
          - listitem:
            - paragraph: Hold & Accept (holds your current call and accepts the new call)
          - listitem:
            - paragraph: Decline (declines the new call)
    - heading "Discover more ways to interact on a FaceTime call" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - paragraph: During a FaceTime call, tap the More button.
      - listitem:
        - paragraph: "Tap any of these options:"
        - list:
          - listitem:
            - paragraph: Add People (adds more people to the current call)
          - listitem:
            - paragraph: Contact Card (opens the other caller's Contact card)
          - listitem:
            - paragraph: Live Captions (shows real-time captions on the current call)
          - listitem:
            - paragraph: Live Translation (translates between languages in real-time)
          - listitem:
            - paragraph: Hold Assist (get notified to pick up when you're no longer on hold)
          - listitem:
            - paragraph: Screen Sharing (shares your screen with the other caller)
          - listitem:
            - paragraph: SharePlay (lets you share movies, workouts, and more on the current call)
    - heading "Find your missed calls, voicemails, and more in FaceTime" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - paragraph: In FaceTime, tap the Filter button in the upper right corner.
        - img "In FaceTime on iPhone, the Filter button is magnified, which can be tapped for in-call options."
      - listitem:
        - paragraph: "Tap any of the options from the list:"
        - list:
          - listitem:
            - paragraph: Calls (your recent FaceTime video and audio calls)
          - listitem:
            - paragraph: Missed (FaceTime video and audio calls that were not answered)
          - listitem:
            - paragraph:
              - text: Video (video messages from other callers)
              - superscript: "4"
          - listitem:
            - paragraph: Voicemail (voicemails from other callers)
          - listitem:
            - paragraph: Unknown Callers (calls from unsaved Contacts)
          - listitem:
            - paragraph: Spam (calls identified as spam or fraud)
          - listitem:
            - paragraph: Manage Filtering (your settings to screen, silence, and filter calls)
    - heading "Get more help" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - paragraph:
          - link "Screen unknown callers on iPhone":
            - /url: https://support.apple.com/en-us/111106
      - listitem:
        - paragraph:
          - link "Use FaceTime on Mac":
            - /url: https://support.apple.com/guide/facetime/welcome/mac
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - paragraph:
          - text: When you tap a person's contact information, FaceTime tries to connect using any FaceTime-enabled numbers or addresses stored for that person. To avoid calling unintended recipients,
          - link "make sure that your contacts are accurate":
            - /url: https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/edit-contacts-iph89a9c71d8/ios
          - text: .
      - listitem:
        - paragraph: "You can use FaceTime on these devices on Wi-Fi: iPhone 4 or later, iPad Pro (all models), iPad 2 or later, and iPad mini (all models)."
      - listitem:
        - paragraph: "With a cellular data plan, you can use FaceTime without Wi-Fi on: iPhone 4s or later, iPad Pro (all models), and iPad (3rd generation or later)."
      - listitem:
        - paragraph:
          - text: If FaceTime detects that certain sensitive content has been sent to a child,
          - link "Communication Safety":
            - /url: https://support.apple.com/en-us/105069
          - text: can warn your child, blur the content, and provide helpful resources.

limitations: Event sequence records provider receipt order; simultaneous browser causality is not inferred.
Network content is retained only when selected; response bytes are browser-decoded, not compressed wire bytes.
Request bytes are limited to what Playwright exposes; not_exposed does not establish body absence or multipart file coverage.
Network content reads settle within 5 seconds each and never wait for unfinished responses or refetch them.
Playwright scenario events do not expose request initiator stacks; receipt order does not prove causality.
Storage values are hashed only after declared-secret redaction.
